STEP 1 - Scene: A plain serving of diced/crumbled white cheese (looks like feta or a soft white cheese, cut into irregular cubes) on a white plate. The other plate at the left edge (carrots, grapes, meat/cheese pieces) is not part of this meal.

STEP 2 - Vessel: Square white plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area ≈ 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2 (treating it as a dinner plate; square corners give a little extra, but the round estimate is adequate).

STEP 3 - Items: one item, diced white cheese (feta-style). No visible oil or dressing.

STEP 4 - Area: the cheese pile covers roughly 30% of the plate's area (it spans about 14 cm across by 10 cm at its widest, with irregular edges). Share of vessel covered by food: ~30%.

STEP 5 - Volume: 30% of 530 cm^2 = 159 cm^2. Pile height averages about 2 cm (a loose heap of cubes), so gross volume ≈ 159 x 2 = 318 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: cheese bulk density ~0.9 g/ml, so 318 x 0.9 ≈ 286 g. Note: this is a loose pile of cubes, so the 0.9 factor already accounts for gaps.

STEP 7 - Energy: feta-style cheese ≈ 264 kcal per 100 g. 286 g x 2.64 ≈ 755 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A heaped ~300 g portion of soft cheese on a dinner plate is plausible for the visible amount. Higher-fat cheeses would push energy up, lower-fat ones down, so this is a reasonable central estimate. Roughly 290 g and about 750 kcal.
